Document Type: Historical Incident Report
Document ID: INC-018
Date: 2026-08-14
Machine ID: Press-04
Batch ID: RB-1988
Defect Type: Surface Crack
Operating Temp: 185.2°C

Incident Description:
Batch RB-1988 experienced a high defect rejection rate (118 rejected units out of 500) due to severe surface micro-cracking. Analysis confirmed that elevated operating temperature of Press-04 (185.2°C) caused thermal expansion strain in plasticized resin.

Lessons Learned & Recommendation:
When Press-04 operates at or above 184°C, surface crack defect rate exponentially increases. Recommend inspecting cooling water lines and re-calibrating temperature sensors immediately whenever temperatures exceed 180°C.

Document Type: Inspection Report
Document ID: IR-RB-2041
Batch ID: RB-2041
Machine ID: Press-04
Date: 2026-09-15
Shift: Shift B
Inspector: Quality Team Lead - Shift B

Batch Summary:
- Production Quantity: 500 units
- Tested Units: 500 units
- Rejected Units: 126 units
- Defect Type Identified: Surface crack / Anomaly
- Recorded Operating Temperature: 184°C
- Recorded Operating Pressure: 72.1 PSI

Inspector Observations:
During Shift B production run, automated visual scanning flagged multiple units from Batch RB-2041 exhibiting linear surface cracking near the neck shoulder. Thermocouple telemetry indicated Press-04 operated at 184°C, which is 4°C above the maximum recommended SOP threshold (180°C). 126 units were rejected prior to packaging. Batch is currently under quarantine pending root-cause investigation.

Document Type: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
Document ID: SOP-PRESS-04
Title: Operational Procedure and Safety Protocol for Molding Press-04
Machine ID: Press-04

1. Machine Specifications & Parameters
- Target Temperature: 170.0°C (Nominal Range: 165.0°C - 175.0°C)
- Maximum Safe Operating Temperature: 180.0°C
- Target Hydraulic Pressure: 70.0 PSI (Nominal Range: 65.0 - 73.0 PSI)
- Line Speed: 42.0 m/min

2. High Temperature Alert Procedure
- WARNING: Operating Press-04 above 180.0°C requires mandatory supervisor sign-off and 100% visual sample inspection.
- High operating temperatures (e.g. 184°C - 188°C) significantly impair resin cooling cycles, resulting in surface cracks, localized warping, and structural weakness in bottle, metal nut, and screw components.
- In case of temperature spike > 180°C:
 a. Immediately inspect thermal control loop thermocouple on Zone 2.
 b. Lower line speed to 38 m/min to allow auxiliary cooling.
 c. Initiate RAG context lookup for recent thermal defect incidents on Press-04.

Document Type: Maintenance Log
Document ID: MAINT-2026-09
Machine ID: Press-04
Date: 2026-09-01
Technician: Senior Maintenance Specialist

Maintenance Summary:
- Cleaned heat exchanger coils.
- Thermocouple calibration checked: Zone 1 calibrated, Zone 2 showing 2.5°C positive thermal drift.
- Hydraulic oil level restored.
- Note: Zone 2 heating element reported slight overheating tendency under high line speeds. Scheduled for full coil replacement in October maintenance window.

Document Type: Quality Manual
Document ID: QM-2026-V4
Title: Standard Quality Management & Defect Escalation Guidelines

1. Purpose and Scope
This document outlines standard quality inspection thresholds, defect classification standards, and mandatory escalation protocols across all production lines including Bottle, Screw, Metal Nut, and Tile molding processes.

2. Temperature Control & Defect Thresholds
- Standard operating temperature range for Press series machines (Press-01 to Press-04) is 165°C to 178°C.
- Operating temperatures exceeding 180°C present a critical thermal risk. Elevated temperatures induce material thermal expansion, localized stress, and surface cracking.
- If a press machine operates above 180°C for more than 10 consecutive minutes, the current production batch MUST be flagged for immediate visual anomaly inspection.

3. Defect Classification Standard
- Surface Anomaly / Micro-cracks: High Severity. Triggers mandatory batch quarantine if defect rate exceeds 1.5%.
- Dimensional Abnormality: Medium Severity. Requires calibration check of hydraulic pressure clamps.
- Texture Deviation: Low Severity. Standard surface finish inspection required.

4. Escalation Protocol
When a batch is flagged with HIGH Risk (Rejection Risk > 70% or Anomaly Score > 0.85):
Step 1: Halt automated packaging for the batch.
Step 2: Cross-reference machine operating temperature against SOP.
Step 3: Review historical incident logs for the active machine ID.
Step 4: Conduct visual sampling using the automated vision inspection system on at least 50 random units.
